name: Which one does Bob mean? (forced choice)
summary: The closed campaign's reference game: participants see a few pictures, Bob says one word or mumbles, and they click the picture they think he means.

charter.question: How do listeners use the alternatives a speaker could have said to pick a referent?

instructions.welcome: In this short study we are interested in how people figure out what others are talking about.
instructions.task: Meet Bob. Bob wants to tell you about some of his things: his friends, his snowmen, the sundaes and pizzas he makes, his boats and his Christmas trees. On each screen you will see a few pictures. Bob can only say one word to tell you which one he means. Click on the picture you think Bob is talking about. Sometimes Bob mumbles and you won't be able to hear his word. Then just click on the one you think he is talking about. There are no right or wrong answers; go with your first impression.

comprehension_checks.question: What do you do on each screen?
options: Click on the picture you think Bob is talking about
Rate how much you like each picture

comprehension_checks.question: How many words can Bob say on each screen?

response.prompt: Bob can only say one word to communicate with you and he says {message}. Click on the one you think Bob is talking about.
response.prior_prompt: Bob can only say one word to communicate with you, but he mumbles: you couldn't hear what he said. Click on the one you think Bob is talking about.
